newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq ready to resume oil export via Syria -minister.
newsitem.headline: Iraq ready to resume oil export via Syria -minister.

text.p: Iraq is ready to resume oil export via the Iraqi-Syrian pipeline, closed since early 1980s, Iraq's Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said on Wednesday.
"We are prepared to resume (oil) pumping via Syria whenever the Syrian government takes a decision to resume pumping," Rasheed said in a press conference.
The Iraqi-Syrian oil pipeline was closed since 1980 when Iraq severed ties with Damscus because Syria sided with Iran in the 1980-88 Iraq-Iran war.
"The decision to stop oil pumping across Syria was Syrian," he said.
But since the last two months there were hints for economic and diplomatic rapprochment between the two neigbouring countries, ruled by rival factions of the Baath party.
Rasheed also said Iraq would support the building of an Iraqi-Jordanian oil pipeline.
"This project is in our mind. It was affirmed in September 1995 and most recently...and we support this project," the oil minister said.
Rasheed gave no further details but said there were "expanding oil cooperation with Jordan whether in securing Jordan's oil needs or offering technical help to improve (Jordanian) oil projects."
Jordan, which is exempt from United Nations sanctions that bar Iraq from freely exporting its oil following its 1990 invasion of Kuwait, imports about 80,000 barrels per day (bpd) from Iraq.
Jordan deposits the funds in an escrow account at its Central Bank and pays almost half of it to finance Jordanian exports to Iraq.
